# DOCX ops

Addressed by the block ids `inspect` reports. An `anchored` id came from a
bookmark and survives insertions above it; an unanchored one is positional and
is only good until the document changes.

## Surgical — available on any document that opened

| op | arguments |
| --- | --- |
| replaceText | `find`, `replace`, `scope` (a block id), `tracked` |
| addComment | `on` (text to anchor to), `text`, `scope` |
| fillPlaceholders | `values {name: string}`, `tracked` |
| setMetadata | `title`, `author`, `subject` |
| insertAfter | `after` (block id), `text`, `style` |
| deleteBlock | `block` |

## Full surface only — an Umbratic document with nothing unsupported

| op | arguments |
| --- | --- |
| replaceBlock | `block`, `text` |
| setHeading | `block`, `level` 1–3 |
| acceptAllChanges | — |
| rejectAllChanges | — |

## Rules

- `tracked: true` writes real `w:ins`/`w:del` revision marks with the
  author from `options.author` and the date. Use it only when the user asked
  for a redline.
- `acceptAllChanges` and `rejectAllChanges` are for finalising, and only
  when the user says to finalise.
- Search coalesces runs first, so a phrase Word split across runs still matches.
- `fillPlaceholders` fails naming any `{{placeholder}}` the document does
  not have.
- One bad op discards the whole batch.
